subject: Technical replicates and Run not recognised

messages.author: 3b0ee05114529dbe
messages.subject: Technical replicates and Run not recognised
parts:
Hi ,

I am running an experiment with 4 conditions with 3 technical replicates and 7 fractions each. he MaxQtoMSstatsFormat() function appears to run smoothly and correctly identifies the fractions, but the dataProcess() function is not recognising any technical replicates. Currently I receive this output:

QuantData <- dataProcess(raw) Warning in dcast.data.table(run_info, GROUP_ORIGINAL + SUBJECT_ORIGINAL ~ : 'fun.aggregate' is NULL, but found duplicate row/column combinations, so defaulting to length(). That is, the variables [GROUP_ORIGINAL, SUBJECT_ORIGINAL, FRACTION] used in 'formula' do not uniquely identify rows in the input 'data'. In such cases, 'fun.aggregate' is used to derive a single representative value for each combination in the output data.table, for example by summing or averaging (fun.aggregate=sum or fun.aggregate=mean, respectively). Check the resulting table for values larger than 1 to see which combinations were not unique. See ?dcast.data.table for more details. INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:23] ** Log2 intensities under cutoff = 11.131 were considered as censored missing values. INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:23] ** Log2 intensities = NA were considered as censored missing values. INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:23] ** Use all features that the dataset originally has. Processed 89487 groups out of 89487. 100% done. Time elapsed: 17s. ETA: 0s. INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:44] # proteins: 8350 # peptides per protein: 1-390 # features per peptide: 1-1 INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:44] Some proteins have only one feature: A0A087X1B6;P10275;F5GZG9;A0A087WUX9;E9PEG3;A0A7I2PS51;P10275-2;P10275-3;P10275-4, A0A0A0MQV6;P09038-2;P09038-3;P09038-1;P09038, A0A140TA09;Q99942, A0A1B0GVT7;O75486;O75486-4, A0A1X7SBW3;Q5TA31 ... INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:44] CNTL FGF2 MCLI MEKI # runs 1 1 1 1 # bioreplicates 1 1 1 1 # tech. replicates 0 0 0 0 INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:45] Some features are completely missing in at least one condition: EEEEQQEGGFASPR_2_NA_NA, EVLFEDR_2_NA_NA, IALGNEASTVQEEEQDR_2_NA_NA, KLQEEYYEEK_2_NA_NA, DVEMGNSVIEENEM(Oxidation (M))K_2_NA_NA ... INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:45] == Start the summarization per subplot... | | 0%Warning in dcast.data.table(LABEL + RUN ~ FEATURE, data = input, value.var = "newABUNDANCE", : 'fun.aggregate' is NULL, but found duplicate row/column combinations, so defaulting to length(). That is, the variables [LABEL, RUN, FEATURE] used in 'formula' do not uniquely identify rows in the input 'data'. In such cases, 'fun.aggregate' is used to derive a single representative value for each combination in the output data.table, for example by summing or averaging (fun.aggregate=sum or fun.aggregate=mean, respectively). Check the resulting table for values larger than 1 to see which combinations were not unique. See ?dcast.data.table for more details. <simpleError in .Primitive("length")(newABUNDANCE, keep = TRUE): 2 arguments passed to 'length' which requires 1> INFO [2024-12-09 14:19:48] == Summarization is done. Warning in merge.data.table(input[, colnames(input) != "newABUNDANCE", with = FALSE], : Input data.table 'y' has no columns. Error in merge.data.table(input[, colnames(input) != "newABUNDANCE", with = FALSE], : Elements listed in `by` must be valid column names in x and y

Could you please guide me on this. Thank you.
